claims.text: The initial cast Co-Cr-Fe-Ni alloy has coarse grains greater than 10 μm and limited ductility.
Adding 0.3–0.5 at.% C and 3–4 at.% Mo, followed by severe deformation and annealing, will stabilize a sub-50 nm FCC+HCP structure.
Vacuum arc melting under Ti-gettered argon and homogenization at 1200 °C are suitable processing steps for the proposed Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Mo-C alloy.
A 70% hot-rolling reduction at 900–1000 °C provides the required severe plastic deformation.
Annealing at 600–700 °C will refine or retain the grains without inducing recrystallization or carbide precipitation.
Carbon and molybdenum segregate to grain boundaries, reduce interfacial energy, and suppress grain growth and grain-boundary sliding.
Metastable FCC/HCP phase boundaries act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Interstitial carbon stabilizes the FCC phase in Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Mo alloys.
Interstitial carbon promotes twinning-induced plasticity.
At concentrations no greater than 4 at.%, Mo provides solid-solution strengthening without precipitating Mo-rich carbides or Laves phases.
An FCC+HCP constitution produces strain hardening through concurrent TRIP and twinning.
Interstitial drag and solute segregation stabilize grains smaller than 50 nm against thermal coarsening.
The processed alloy will have yield strength above 750 MPa and tensile strength above 1100 MPa.
The processed alloy will retain elongation above 60%.
No brittle Mo-rich carbides or Laves phases will be detectable by XRD or SEM in the target composition range.
The unmodified cast baseline has grain sizes of 17–47 μm.
Mo contents above 4 at.% cause Mo4C precipitation.
Carbon contents above 0.5 at.% may eliminate the HCP phase or induce carbide formation.
Annealing above the nanocrystalline stability limit causes grain growth or transformation to brittle phases.
Mechanical testing is to be conducted at a strain rate of 1 × 10^-3 s^-1.

contradictions.description: Formation of Mo4C or Laves phases above 4 at.% Mo is defined as expected behavior outside the stated stability boundary, but the same behavior is labeled as falsification of the hypothesis. Testing an explicitly excluded composition does not decisively falsify the claim restricted to 3–4 at.% Mo.
